'''Jarrod Reed Uthoff''' (born May 19, 1993) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Petkim Spor]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL). He played three seasons of [[college basketball]] for the [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa Hawkeyes]].

==High school career==
Uthoff starred at [[Jefferson High School (Cedar Rapids, Iowa)|Jefferson High School]] in Cedar Rapids, earning [[Iowa Mr. Basketball]] honors as the top high school player in the state as a senior in 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.metrosportsreport.com/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=1588:uthoff-is-mr-basketball&catid=184:about-msr|title=Jarrod Uthoff is Iowa's Mr. Basketball|work=MetroSportsReport.com|date=March 15, 2011|access-date=January 5, 2016}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Jarrod Uthoff.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Uthoff during his time with the [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa Hawkeyes]].]]
Uthoff committed to the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison|University of Wisconsin]], where he sat out the 2011–12 season as a [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]]. He decided to transfer in the off-season. His case received national press as Wisconsin coach [[Bo Ryan]] originally barred the player from transferring to 26 different schools. After heavy public scrutiny, Ryan reduced his restrictions to only cover the [[Big Ten Conference]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Rob|last=Dauster|url=http://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2012/04/22/jarrod-uthoff-finally-shares-his-side-of-the-story/|title=Jarrod Uthoff finally shares his side of the story|work=NBCSports.com|date=April 25, 2012|access-date=January 5, 2016}}</ref> Uthoff ultimately chose Iowa, a Big Ten school, opting to pay his own way in the 2012–13 season as he sat out the year as a transfer per [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] regulations.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/otl/story/_/id/8018874/jarrod-uthoff-transferring-wisconsin-badgers-iowa-hawkeyes|title=Jarrod Uthoff to transfer to Iowa|work=ESPN.com|date=June 7, 2012|access-date=January 5, 2016}}</ref>

Uthoff finally took the court for the Hawkeyes in 2013–14 season as a redshirt [[sophomore]]. He was a key player off the bench for the team, averaging 7.6 [[Points per game|points]] and 4.6 [[rebounds per game]]. With graduation losses the following season, he entered the starting lineup. As a junior, he averaged 12.4 points and 6.4 rebounds per game as a complement to senior forward [[Aaron White (basketball)|Aaron White]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Scott|last=Dochterman|url=http://www.thegazette.com/subject/sports/iowas-uthoff-humble-but-confident-20150703|title=Iowa's Uthoff humble but confident|work=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]]|date=July 3, 2015|access-date=January 5, 2016}}</ref> At the close of the year, Uthoff was named third-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kcci.com/sports/iowas-white-uthoff-earn-allbig-ten-distinction/31704806|title=Iowa's White, Uthoff Earn All-Big Ten Distinction|work=KCCI.com|date=March 9, 2015|access-date=January 5, 2016}}</ref>

Leading up to his senior season, Uthoff was named to the preseason All-Big Ten team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/101415aab.html|title=Big Ten Men's Basketball Preseason Honors Announced|work=[[Big Ten Conference]]|date=October 14, 2015|access-date=January 5, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151016190850/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/101415aab.html|archive-date=October 16, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> With the departure of Aaron White, Uthoff stepped into the role of the Hawkeyes' top scoring option.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jon|last=Rothstein|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/25408689/observations-iowas-jarrod-uthoff-has-been-a-key-player-for-hawkeyes|title=Observations: Iowa's Jarrod Uthoff has been a key player for Hawkeyes|work=CBSSports.com|date=December 10, 2015|access-date=January 5, 2016}}</ref> He was named to the 35-man midseason watchlist for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Trophy]] on February 11.<ref>{{cite news|first=Terrence|last=Payne|title=Naismith Trophy midseason list announced|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/oklahoma-sooners-buddy-hield-lsu-tigers-ben-simmons-naismith-trophy-35-finalists-021116|work=[[Fox Sports]]|date=February 11, 2016|access-date=February 19, 2016}}</ref> Over his three-year career, he averaged 13.0 points, 5.8 rebounds and 1.7 blocks in 100 games. He finished his collegiate career ranked 19th all-time in Hawkeyes scoring (1,298 points), fourth in blocked shots (177) and 10th in three-pointers made (137).

==Professional career==
===Raptors 905 (2016–2017)===
After going undrafted in the [[2016 NBA draft]], Uthoff joined the [[Sacramento Kings]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa/basketball-men/2016/06/25/jarrod-uthoff-sacramento-kings-nba-summer-league/86383044/|title=Jarrod Uthoff Finds Destination for NBA Summer League|work=[[Des Moines Register]]|date=June 25, 2016|access-date=June 25, 2016}}</ref> On August 2, 2016, he signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/press-releases/uthoff-080216|title=Raptors Sign Jarrod Uthoff|work=NBA.com|date=August 2, 2016|access-date=August 2, 2016}}</ref> but was waived on October 22 after appearing in one preseason game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/press-releases/roster-102216|title=Raptors Release Five From Roster|work=NBA.com|date=October 22, 2016|access-date=October 22, 2016}}</ref> On October 30, he was acquired by [[Raptors 905]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of the Raptors.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://raptors905.dleague.nba.com/news/training-camp-roster-schedule/|title=TRAINING CAMP ROSTER AND SCHEDULE|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=October 30, 2016|access-date=November 2, 2016|archive-date=November 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161104011449/http://raptors905.dleague.nba.com/news/training-camp-roster-schedule/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On January 27, 2017, he was traded to the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://raptors905.dleague.nba.com/news/raptors-905-acquire-christian-watford-fort-wayne/|title=RAPTORS 905 ACQUIRE CHRISTIAN WATFORD FROM FORT WAYNE|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=January 27, 2017|access-date=January 31, 2017|archive-date=February 3, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170203185342/http://raptors905.dleague.nba.com/news/raptors-905-acquire-christian-watford-fort-wayne/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Dallas Mavericks (2017)===
On March 9, 2017, Uthoff signed a 10-day contract with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-manny-harris-and-jarrod-uthoff-to-10-day-contracts/|title=Mavericks sign Manny Harris and Jarrod Uthoff to 10-day contracts|work=Mavs.com|date=March 9, 2017|access-date=March 9, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://sportsday.dallasnews.com/dallas-mavericks/mavericks/2017/03/08/mavericks-reported-signing-ofjarrod-uthoff-likely-means-ben-bentil|title=What Mavericks' reported signing of Jarrod Uthoff likely means for Ben Bentil|access-date=March 10, 2017|date=March 8, 2017|work=[[Dallas News]]|author=Townsend, Brad}}</ref> He made his NBA debut the following day in the Mavericks' 105–96 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]], playing two minutes off the bench.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400900366|title=Nets vs. Mavericks – Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=March 10, 2017|access-date=March 10, 2017}}</ref> On March 19, 2017, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Mavericks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/mavericks-jarrod-uthoff-inks-second-10-day-contract-with-mavericks/|title=Mavericks' Jarrod Uthoff: Inks second 10-day contract with Mavericks|work=CBSSports.com|date=March 19, 2017|access-date=March 29, 2017}}</ref> During his first 20 days as a Maverick, he received two assignments to the [[Texas Legends]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Texas-Legends/32/Transaction_History/2017|title=2016–2017 Texas Legends Transactions History|work=RealGM.com|access-date=March 27, 2017}}</ref> On March 29, 2017, he signed a multi-year contract with the Mavericks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavs-sign-jarrod-uthoff-to-multi-year-deal/|title=Mavs sign Jarrod Uthoff to multi-year deal|work=Mavs.com|date=March 29, 2017|access-date=March 29, 2017}}</ref>

On June 29, 2017, Uthoff was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in exchange for cash considerations.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=20466|title=Mavericks trade Jarrod Uthoff to Rockets|work=InsideHoops.com|date=June 29, 2017|access-date=June 29, 2017}}</ref> On July 31, 2017, Uthoff was waived by the Rockets.

===Fort Wayne Mad Ants (2017–2018)===
In the 2017–18 season with the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]], Uthoff averaged 16.5 points, 8.4 rebounds, and 2.5 assists per game.<ref>{{cite news|title=Final 2017–18 NBA G League stats for ex-Iowa collegians|url=http://www.thegazette.com/final-nba-g-league-stats-for-ex-iowa-collegians-20180327|access-date=May 21, 2018|work=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]]|date=March 27, 2018}}</ref>

===Zenit Saint Petersburg (2018–2019)===
On July 19, 2018, Uthoff signed with [[BC Zenit Saint Petersburg|Zenit Saint Petersburg]] of the [[VTB United League]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Zenit announces Jarrod Uthoff|url=https://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/8vt6b6jkojlomecp/zenit-announces-jarrod-uthoff|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180821160339/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/8vt6b6jkojlomecp/zenit-announces-jarrod-uthoff|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 21, 2018|access-date=October 16, 2019|work=EurocupBasketball.com|date=October 16, 2019}}</ref> where he played 16 games and averaged 7.2 points, 3.4 rebounds and 0.6 assists in 16.3 minutes.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jarrod Uthoff International Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/international/players/jarrod-uthoff-1.html|access-date=October 16, 2019|work=Basketball-Reference.com}}</ref>

===Memphis Hustle (2019–2020)===
On October 16, 2019, Uthoff was signed by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] of the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Jarrod Uthoff|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-jarrod-uthoff-191016|access-date=October 16, 2019|work=NBA.com|date=October 16, 2019}}</ref> and waived the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Shaq Buchanan|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-shaq-buchanan-191017|access-date=October 17, 2019|work=NBA.com|date=October 17, 2019}}</ref> He was added to the roster of the Grizzlies’ G League affiliate, the [[Memphis Hustle]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Langham |first1=Geoff |title=Memphis Hustle announce final roster |url=https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/memphis-hustle-announce-final-roster-191104/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 5, 2019 |date=November 4, 2019 |archive-date=November 7, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191107023529/https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/memphis-hustle-announce-final-roster-191104/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> On December 31, Uthoff tallied 30 points, nine rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block in a 128–113 win over the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Jarrod Uthoff: Scores 30 points in 28 minutes |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jarrod-uthoff-scores-30-points-in-28-minutes/ |access-date=January 13, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 1, 2020}}</ref> Uthoff was named Midseason All-NBA G League for the Western Conference.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.desototimes.com/sports/four-hustle-players-on-g-league-midseason-team/article_d819a24c-4c50-11ea-96c9-f7e7fd313fa1.html|title=Four Hustle players on G League midseason team|first=Bob|last=Bakken|work=DeSoto Times-Tribune|date=February 10, 2020|access-date=February 12, 2020}}</ref>

===Memphis Grizzlies (2020)===
On February 27, 2020, Uthoff signed a 10-day contract with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].  His contract expired on March 7, 2020.  He appeared in four games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-jarrod-uthoff-to-10-day-contract-200227|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Jarrod Uthoff to 10-day contract|work=NBA.com|date=February 27, 2020|access-date=February 27, 2020}}</ref>  The G League season was canceled, due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], before Uthoff could rejoin the Hustle.

===Washington Wizards (2020)===
On July 17, 2020, at the beginning of the "[[2020 NBA Bubble|Orlando Bubble]]" phase of the pandemic-interrupted [[2019-2020 NBA season]], the [[Washington Wizards]] signed Uthoff to a "substitution contract." He filled a roster sport vacated by [[Gary Payton II]], who had tested positive for [[COVID-19]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Wizards sign Jarrod Uthoff|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-sign-jarrod-uthoff|date=July 17, 2020|website=NBA.com |access-date=July 17, 2020}}</ref> Uthoff remained with the team until the end of the season, appearing in three games.  The Wizards did not qualify for the playoffs.

===Erie BayHawks (2021)===
On December 2, 2020, Uthoff signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Pelicans sign four players|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-four-players|date=December 2, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 2, 2020}}</ref> On December 19, 2020, Uthoff was waived by the Pelicans at the end of training camp.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pelicans waive four|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-waive-four|date=December 19, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 19, 2020}}</ref>

Uthoff's [[NBA G League|G League]] rights were still held by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]' affiliate, the [[Memphis Hustle]], when he was waived by the Pelicans. Uthoff was unable to join the Pelicans' affiliate [[Birmingham Squadron|Erie BayHawks]] until the BayHawks made a deal to trade the 2nd overall draft pick in the [[2021 NBA G League draft (January)|2021 NBA G League draft]] to the Hustle.<ref>{{cite web|first1=Corey|last1=Moore|title=Memphis Hustle complete trade with Erie BayHawks|url=https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/memphis-hustle-complete-trade-with-erie-bayhawks-210111|date=January 11, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 11, 2021}}</ref> The draft was held on January 11, 2021, and Memphis used the pick to acquire [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] forward [[Freddie Gillespie]].<ref>{{cite web|first1=Corey|last1=Moore|title=Memphis Hustle acquire two players in 2020–21 NBA G League draft|url=https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/memphis-hustle-acquire-two-players-in-2020-21-nba-g-league-draft-210111|date=January 11, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 11, 2021}}</ref>

The BayHawks were one of 18 teams who played the [[2020–21 NBA G League season|2021 G League season]] in a "bubble" at [[Walt Disney World]], beginning in February.<ref>{{cite web| title=Trade with Memphis Hustle gives Erie BayHawks returning player rights to Jarrod Uthoff|date=January 11, 2021|url=https://www.yourerie.com/sports/local-sports/trade-with-memphis-hustle-gives-erie-bayhawks-returning-player-rights-to-jarrod-uthoff|access-date= January 12, 2021}}</ref> On January 12, 2021, Uthoff was included in the roster of the [[Birmingham Squadron|Erie BayHawks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Erie BayHawks announce 2021 roster|url=https://erie.gleague.nba.com/news/erie-bayhawks-announce-2021-roster|date=January 12, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 12, 2021|archive-date=February 14, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220214211047/https://erie.gleague.nba.com/news/erie-bayhawks-announce-2021-roster/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He played in and started 14 of the BayHawks' 15 games, averaging 8.8 rebounds and 14.9 points per game. The Bayhawks went 11–4 and made the playoffs, but got knocked out in the first round. Uthoff was named a Third Team G League All-Star at the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://erie.gleague.nba.com/news/bayhawks-jarrod-uthoff-named-all-nba-g-league-third-team/|title=Bayhawks Jarrod Uthoff Named to All-Nba G League Third Team|access-date=April 1, 2021|archive-date=March 25, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210325003909/https://erie.gleague.nba.com/news/bayhawks-jarrod-uthoff-named-all-nba-g-league-third-team/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===SeaHorses Mikawa (2021–2022)===
On June 23, 2021, Uthoff signed with [[SeaHorses Mikawa]] of the [[B.League]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Jarrod Uthoff joins Japanese team SeaHorses |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/jarrod-uthoff-joins-japanese-team-seahorses/ |website=Sportando |access-date=June 23, 2021 |date=June 23, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=選手加入のお知らせ(ジェロード・ユトフ選手)|url=https://go-seahorses.jp/news/detail/id=17140|access-date=2021-06-26|website=シーホース三河|language=ja}}</ref> On February 19, 2022, Uthoff was traded from the [[Birmingham Squadron]] to the [[Austin Spurs]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021–22 NBA G League Transactions|date=February 19, 2022|access-date=February 19, 2022}}</ref> but he remained in Japan, continuing to play for Mikawa.

===Pallacanestro Trieste (2024–2026)===
On July 27, 2024, he signed with [[Pallacanestro Trieste]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pallacanestrotrieste.it/jarrod-uthoff-e-biancorosso/|title=Jarrod Uthoff È Biancorosso|last=|first=|date=July 27, 2024|website=pallacanestrotrieste.it|publisher=|language=it|access-date=August 17, 2024}}</ref>

===Petkim Spor (2026–present)===
On July 3, 2026, he signed with [[Petkim Spor]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).<ref>{{Cite tweet |user=Petkimspor |number=2072945784371200469 |title=Ailemize hoş geldin Jarrod Uthoff!}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Uthoff majored in economics at the University of Iowa.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hawkeyesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jarrod_uthoff_815339.html |title=Iowa Hawkeyes bio |work=HawkeyeSports.com |access-date=October 22, 2016 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160626153908/http://www.hawkeyesports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jarrod_uthoff_815339.html |archive-date=June 26, 2016 }}</ref> His third cousin, [[Dean Uthoff]], played basketball at [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]] and then went on to play professionally in Australia. An [[National Basketball League (Australia)|Australian National Basketball League]] legend, Dean played 13 years in the league for the [[Nunawading Spectres]] and then the [[Sydney Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Mike|last=Hlas|url=http://www.thegazette.com/subject/sports/hlas-jarrod-isnt-first-uthoff-to-make-good-in-basketball-20160115|title=Hlas: Jarrod isn't first Uthoff to make good in basketball|work=[[The Gazette (Cedar Rapids)|The Gazette]] |date=January 15, 2016|access-date=April 12, 2017}}</ref> Dean's brother, Ed, also distinguished himself in college ball and was team captain at San Jose State.

Uthoff is married to Jessie Jordan Uthoff, daughter of congressman [[Jim Jordan]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Chad|last=Leistikow|url=https://www.hawkcentral.com/story/sports/college/iowa/basketball-men/2016/02/29/inside-jarrod-uthoff-hawkeyes-senior-day/81101720/|title=Jarrod Uthoff on faith, love, basketball and his Iowa legacy|work=hawkcentral.com |date=February 29, 2016|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref>
